entities.name: Alkyl azide reduction
observations: Net transformation is terminal alkyl azide (–CH2–N3) to primary amine (–CH2–NH2); the fused scaffold and carbonyl groups are retained.

entities.name: Alkyl azide
observations: The reactant contains a primary alkyl azide substituent, represented as –CH2–N=[N+]=[N−].

entities.name: Primary amine
observations: The product contains the corresponding primary alkyl amine, represented as –CH2–NH2.

entities.name: Azide hydrogenation
observations: Catalytic hydrogenation is a plausible reagent class for reducing an alkyl azide to a primary amine; common systems include H2 with Pd/C, PtO2, or Raney Ni.

entities.name: Staudinger reduction
observations: A phosphine such as triphenylphosphine or trimethylphosphine, often followed by aqueous workup, is an alternative reagent class for converting an alkyl azide to a primary amine.
